## Solution

**Notation.** The numerator $N(t)=\int_{0}^{\sqrt t}\!\Bigl(\int_{x^{2}}^{t}\sin(y^{2})\,dy\Bigr)dx$ depends only on $t$. The denominator depends on the free variable $x$ (and $t$). We take $x\to+\infty$ first, then $t\to0^{+}$.

---

### Step 1. Inner limit: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to+\infty}\Bigl(\tfrac{2}{\pi}\arctan\tfrac{x}{t^{2}}\Bigr)^{x}$ (fixed $t>0$)

Set $u=x/t^{2}\to\infty$. Using $\arctan u=\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\tfrac{1}{u}+O(u^{-3})$,

$$\frac{2}{\pi}\arctan\frac{x}{t^{2}}=1-\frac{2t^{2}}{\pi x}+O(x^{-3}).$$

Hence

$$x\ln\!\Bigl(\frac{2}{\pi}\arctan\frac{x}{t^{2}}\Bigr)=x\Bigl(-\frac{2t^{2}}{\pi x}+O(x^{-2})\Bigr)=-\frac{2t^{2}}{\pi}+O(x^{-1})\;\longrightarrow\;-\frac{2t^{2}}{\pi},$$

so

$$\lim_{x\to+\infty}\Bigl(\frac{2}{\pi}\arctan\frac{x}{t^{2}}\Bigr)^{x}=e^{-2t^{2}/\pi}.$$

Therefore the denominator (after the inner limit) becomes

$$D(t)=\bigl(e^{-2t^{2}/\pi}-1\bigr)\,\arctan(t^{3/2}).$$

---

### Step 2. Asymptotics of the denominator as $t\to0^{+}$

$$e^{-2t^{2}/\pi}-1=-\frac{2t^{2}}{\pi}+O(t^{4}),\qquad \arctan(t^{3/2})=t^{3/2}+O(t^{9/2}).$$

Thus

$$D(t)=-\frac{2}{\pi}\,t^{7/2}+O(t^{9/2}).$$

---

### Step 3. Asymptotics of the numerator as $t\to0^{+}$

For small $y$, $\sin(y^{2})=y^{2}+O(y^{6})$. The leading term is

$$N(t)=\int_{0}^{\sqrt t}\int_{x^{2}}^{t}y^{2}\,dy\,dx+O(t^{11/2}).$$

Compute the leading double integral:

$$\int_{0}^{\sqrt t}\frac{t^{3}-x^{6}}{3}\,dx=\frac{1}{3}\Bigl[t^{3}\sqrt t-\frac{(\sqrt t)^{7}}{7}\Bigr]=\frac{1}{3}\Bigl[t^{7/2}-\frac{t^{7/2}}{7}\Bigr]=\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{6}{7}\,t^{7/2}=\frac{2}{7}\,t^{7/2}.$$

Hence

$$N(t)=\frac{2}{7}\,t^{7/2}+O(t^{11/2}).$$

---

### Step 4. The limit

$$I=\lim_{t\to0^{+}}\frac{N(t)}{D(t)}=\lim_{t\to0^{+}}\frac{\frac{2}{7}\,t^{7/2}+O(t^{11/2})}{-\frac{2}{\pi}\,t^{7/2}+O(t^{9/2})}=\frac{2/7}{-2/\pi}=-\frac{\pi}{7}.$$

---

$$\boxed{I=-\dfrac{\pi}{7}}$$

Let $a = \frac{2}{\pi}\arctan\frac{x}{t^2}$. As $x\to\infty$, $a\to 1^-$.

$\ln a = \ln\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\arctan\frac{x}{t^2}\right)$.
